neet_che_u17_t05_1.working: The O atom is sp3, but repulsion between the bulky methyl groups widens the angle beyond 109.5°, to about 111.7°.

neet_che_u17_t05_2.working: The Ar–O bond has partial double-bond character, so it is not cleaved. Iodide attacks the methyl carbon (SN2), giving phenol and CH3I.

neet_che_u17_t05_3.working: Ethers have no O–H bond, so they cannot H-bond with each other and their boiling points are low. Their oxygen lone pairs can accept H-bonds from water, which makes them soluble.

neet_che_u17_t05_4.working: A matches 111.7° (III), B matches 141 pm (I), C matches sp3 (II), and D matches phenol + CH3I (IV).

neet_che_u17_t05_5.working: A is true. B is false because ethers are polar (the bent shape leaves a net dipole). C is true because lone-pair delocalisation shortens Ar–O. D is false because the O–CH3 bond breaks. E is true. The correct set is A, C and E.
